minde

/ˈmin.dɛ/ verb · Lojban

To command a desktop through live, inspectable Scheme.

— Lojban gismu minde: to command; x1 orders x2 to do x3.

Minde is a Wayland compositor for people who want to understand and alter the machinery they use all day. Smithay owns the protocol, rendering, and input; Guile owns policy. Inspect it, redefine it, or drive it over local IPC while the session is alive.

1. evaluate — keymaps, hooks, placement, groups, and frames are live Guile procedures; behavior changes without restarting the session.

2. compose — groups, heads, and explicit frames instead of a fixed layout algorithm; the window model descends from StumpWM.

3. interrogate — the local IPC interface exposes state, evaluation, status, and structured events to scripts and Eww.

4. hack, safely — the nested backend exercises the real policy layer without touching DRM, your VT, or the display manager.

usage

guix shell -m manifest.scm
scripts/run-nested
